lines.japanese: 祥玄社の入っているビジネスビルの地上１階。だだっ広い吹き抜けの底にて、友人の到着を待つ鷲介くん。
lines.english: The first floor of the office building that houses Shougensha. At the bottom of its enormous atrium, young Shuusuke waits for his friend to arrive.

lines.japanese: ガラス越しに見る土曜のオフィス街はゴーストタウンのごとく人通り少なく、植え込みの潅木を揺らす風の音さえここまで聞こえてきそうです。
lines.english: Through the glass, the Saturday business district has as few pedestrians as a ghost town. I almost expect to hear the wind shaking the shrubs outside all the way from here.

lines.japanese: 俺は隅っこのコーヒーテーブルに入口側を向いて座り、頂いたばかりの本を開いておりました。
lines.english: I sat at a coffee table in the corner, facing the entrance, with the book I'd just been given open in front of me.

lines.japanese: まだ５ページちょっと目を通したところですけどね、なかなか面白いんですよ、これが。
lines.english: I'd only read a little over five pages, but it was pretty interesting.

lines.japanese: のっけから過激な性描写で始まり、毒気あるのに憎めないユーモラスな語り口で豊胸手術にまつわる悲喜こもごもを語りつつ、初めての現場に向かうロケバスでの心情をセンチメンタルに綴って一区切り。
lines.english: It opened straight off with a graphic sex scene, then recounted the joys and sorrows of breast augmentation in a humorous voice that was biting yet hard to dislike, before closing the section with a sentimental account of her feelings on the location bus to her first shoot.

lines.japanese: ふむふむ。すぐ読みおわっちゃいそうだし、誉めるのにも困らないみたいだし、これはおいしい仕事をもらったなあ。
lines.english: Hmm, hmm. Looks like I'll finish it in no time, and I won't have trouble praising it either. This is a pretty sweet assignment.

lines.japanese: ふと次の章へうつる前に頭を上げると、やたら脚の長い美男子がのたのたやってくるところでした。
lines.english: Looking up before starting the next chapter, I saw a handsome man with extraordinarily long legs ambling toward me.

lines.japanese: 彼は無言のままジャケットを脱いで、俺の向かいの席にどすんと腰を下ろしました。
lines.english: Without a word, he took off his jacket and dropped heavily into the chair opposite mine.

lines.japanese: 「えーと……遅かったね？」
lines.english: “Uh... You're late?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、先に帰っててよかったのに。俺、行くとは言ったけど、待ってろとは言ってないよ」
lines.english: “Oh, you could've gone home. I said I was coming, not that you had to wait.”

lines.japanese: 悪びれもせず、むしろ逆ギレ気味な態度。そらまあ、言ってることは間違ってないですけど──ええ、まあ、これがカケルくんという男の子なんです。
lines.english: Not a trace of remorse. If anything, he sounded annoyed at me. Well, sure, what he'd said wasn't wrong—but yes, that's the boy we call Kakeru.

lines.japanese: このようにして彼は、あの見えざる敵対勢力を築いてきたのでしょう。でも俺は、彼がただの照れ屋さんだと思っているので（思いたいじゃないですか）いちいち腹を立てたりはしません。
lines.english: This must be how he built up that invisible hostile force. But I think he's just shy—wouldn't you like to think so?—so I don't get mad over every little thing.

lines.japanese: 「や、気にしないで。待つってより読書してただけだし」
lines.english: “No, don't worry. I wasn't so much waiting as reading.”

lines.japanese: そう言ってハードカバーを立てて見せ、無為に時間を過ごしていたわけじゃないことをアピールしてあげます。どうよコレ。優しいでしょ？
lines.english: I held up the hardcover to show I hadn't been wasting my time. How's that? Nice of me, right?

lines.japanese: 「きのうオールでさ。や、ツルんでた連中がいろいろ面倒起こしちゃって大変だったんだよね。今日は今日で、夜ンなったらひとイベントありそうだし。俺、いつ寝りゃいいんだよ」
lines.english: “I was out all night yesterday. The guys I was with got into all kinds of trouble. What a pain. And there's another little event coming up tonight. When the hell am I supposed to sleep?”

lines.japanese: カケルくんは「ごめん」を省いて寝坊した理由だけ説明しました。どうやらご機嫌ななめのようです──っても、基本的にオールウェイズ機嫌悪げなんで、ちょっと分かりにくいですけどね。
lines.english: Skipping the “sorry,” Kakeru explained only why he'd overslept. Apparently, he was in a bad mood—though he basically always looks like he's in a bad mood, so it's a little hard to tell.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、素敵だわ。カケルくんったらお友達の面倒見がいいのね」
lines.english: “Why, how wonderful. You're so good at looking after your friends, Kakeru.”

lines.japanese: 彼がそんな言葉で気を良くするはずはないんですが、ご存知のとおり、俺は気が付いた他人の美徳はすぐ口にしたくなるタチなのです。
lines.english: Those words were hardly going to improve his mood, but as you know, I'm the sort who wants to mention other people's virtues the moment I notice them.

lines.japanese: 「や、そんなんじゃなくて。あいつら、ハナっから俺だのみで無計画に暴れ放題……ま、いいや。シュウちゃんには関係ない話だよ」
lines.english: “No, it's not like that. They counted on me from the start and went wild without planning a damn thing... Whatever. Nothing to do with you, Shuu.”

lines.japanese: 「えーなに、その面白げなエピソード予告編。教えてくれたっていーんじゃないの、待たせた相手にぐらいさー」
lines.english: “Aww, what's that interesting little preview? You could tell me, couldn't you? At least tell the guy you kept waiting.”

lines.japanese: 「待ってたんじゃなくて本読んでただけ、つったじゃん」
lines.english: “You said you weren't waiting, you were reading.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、それはそれとしてさ。ほら、事実は小説よりストレンジ？」
lines.english: “Well, aside from that. You know, truth is stranger than fiction?”

lines.japanese: しかしながらカケルくんは、突撃レポーターの追及をかわす芸能人みたいに無言で手を振るだけでした。
lines.english: But Kakeru just waved a hand without a word, like a celebrity dodging a pushy reporter's questions.

lines.japanese: ひとが何かを言いかけてやめるとき、本当は聞いてもらいたいがゆえってこともあるものですが、この場合はそういうわけでもなさそうです。
lines.english: Sometimes people start to say something, then stop because they secretly want you to ask. But that didn't seem to be the case here.

lines.japanese: かと言っていきなり口をつぐむのもそれはそれで空気が悪くなりそうなので、俺はあいだを取って、少しだけ話題を逸らすことにしました。
lines.english: On the other hand, suddenly shutting up might sour the mood too. I decided on a compromise and shifted the topic slightly.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに、そのお友達ってどーゆーアレ？」
lines.english: “By the way, what's the, y'know, deal with these friends?”

lines.japanese: なんとなくそんなことを尋ねたのは、米田さんの口にしていた噂が意外と気になっていたからかもしれません。
lines.english: Maybe I casually asked because the rumors Yuu had mentioned bothered me more than I'd expected.

lines.japanese: 「アレって、なにが」
lines.english: “What ‘deal’?”

lines.japanese: 「なに繋がり？　ガッコー時代の同級生とか、仕事仲間のハンサムとか？」
lines.english: “How do you know them? Old classmates? Handsome guys from work?”

lines.japanese: 「とか？言われても。いろいろいるから、んな、いちいち」
lines.english: “What's with ‘or this, or that’? There's all kinds. I'm not listing every one.”

lines.japanese: あ、言いたくなさそうですねこりゃ。またの機会にしましょう。
lines.english: Ah, looks like he doesn't want to talk. Another time, then.

lines.japanese: 「カケルさんったらお友達が多いのね。それはとても素敵なことだわ」
lines.english: “You have so many friends, Kakeru. That's a wonderful thing.”

lines.japanese: 「世の中には虎の威を借りたがる狐が多いってことでしょ」
lines.english: “Just means there are plenty of foxes who want to borrow a tiger's claws.”

lines.japanese: 「いやだわ。それは有名人ゆえの被害妄想じゃないかしら」
lines.english: “Oh, dear. Could that be the paranoia of the famous?”

lines.japanese: 終始うつむきがちだったカケルくんが、ゆっくり頭をもたげました。
lines.english: Kakeru, who'd been looking down most of this time, slowly raised his head.

lines.japanese: 「シュウちゃんって……平和だよね」
lines.english: “Shuu... You're so peaceful.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いま溜息ついた？」
lines.english: “Oh, did you just sigh?”

lines.japanese: 「なんていうか、平和讃歌が具現化したみたいな存在？」
lines.english: “Like... a hymn to peace given human form?”

lines.japanese: 「ついたよね、フッて。鼻でブレスしたよね」
lines.english: “You did, didn't you? That little huff. You breathed through your nose.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 逃げるように横を向いたカケルくんが、ぼそりと一言つぶやきました。
lines.english: Turning aside as if making an escape, Kakeru muttered a word.

lines.japanese: 「タマイズミだ」
lines.english: “Tamaizumi.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 不意に飛びだしたそれは覚えたての人名。
lines.english: The name he'd suddenly let slip sounded like one I'd just learned.

lines.japanese: カケルくんの視線を追って首を４５度曲げれば、わりと空いてるカフェの一席に、読書に耽るひとりの綺麗な娘さんがおりました。
lines.english: Following his gaze, I turned my head forty-five degrees. At a table in the fairly empty café, a pretty girl was absorbed in a book.

lines.japanese: 見た感じビジネス街に溶けこむにはまだ早い若さですが、白いティーカップにそっと口をつける姿そこだけを切りとって見れば、実に絵になる美少女の午後といった体です。
lines.english: She looked a little too young to blend into the business district, but isolate the way she gently sipped from her white teacup, and you had a perfect picture of a beautiful girl's afternoon.

lines.japanese: コンサバって言うんでしょうか、キレイ目の服装。ノンフレームの眼鏡が似合う知的な面立ち。控えめにシャギーされた毛先は、肩のあたりで揃いすぎず不揃いすぎず、なんとも絶妙な塩梅です。
lines.english: Conservative, I guess you'd call it? A neat outfit. An intelligent face well suited to frameless glasses. Lightly layered ends fell around her shoulders, neither too even nor too uneven, in a wonderfully subtle balance.

lines.japanese: 彼女はまっすぐ背筋を伸ばした、ともすれば見てる方が疲れてきそうな姿勢で、テーブルすれすれに浮かせた文庫本へと目を落としておりました。
lines.english: Her back was so straight that just looking at her posture might tire you out. Her eyes were lowered to a paperback held just above the table.

lines.japanese: かっちりした折り目正しいそのさまは、ポストモダン建築の高層ビルにそそぐ柔らかな晩秋の陽射しを受けて、きりりと崇高でやんごとない雰囲気を漂わせています。
lines.english: That crisp, proper figure, bathed in the soft late-autumn sunlight falling on the postmodern high-rise, radiated a dignified, lofty, almost aristocratic air.

lines.japanese: 「え、タマイヅミってたしか……」
lines.english: “Huh, Tama... Izumi... wasn't that...”

lines.japanese: 俺は椅子の上で自分のバッグを開き、しまったばかりの本を慌てて引っぱりだして──
lines.english: Still in my chair, I opened my bag and hurriedly pulled out the book I'd just put away—

lines.japanese: 「多摩いづみ！？」
lines.english: “Izumi Tama?!”

lines.japanese: ──表紙に書かれていた著者名を、声に出して読みあげました。
lines.english: —and read the author's name on the cover aloud.

lines.japanese: 「あれが……や、あちらの方が？」
lines.english: “That's... I mean, that's her?”

lines.japanese: 俺が驚いたのは偶然の出会いにというより、その予想に反するいづみ先生のお姿にです。
lines.english: What surprised me wasn't so much the chance encounter as how different Ms. Tama looked from anything I'd imagined.

lines.japanese: や、そんな予想とかべつにしてたわけではないんですけど、およそ経歴や作風からイメージしうるジャラジャラした女性像からは掛けはなれていました。
lines.english: Not that I'd actually imagined anything, but she was a far cry from the flashy, jangling sort of woman her background and writing might bring to mind.

lines.japanese: なにしろご覧の通り、いまテーブルみっつ隔てた席で静かに読書しているその少女は、グランドピアノやゴールデンレトリバーの似合ういいとこのお嬢さん（お嬢様まではいかない）って感じなのです。
lines.english: As you can see, the girl quietly reading three tables away looked like a young lady from a good family—not quite a princess—who'd suit a grand piano and a golden retriever.

lines.japanese: 「やー、びっくり。ほーんと、人間って生き物は実に奥が深いわあ」
lines.english: “Wow, what a surprise. People really do have such depths.”

lines.japanese: 英字新聞柄のブックカバーが似合うその理知的なお姿を眺めながら、彼女の波乱に満ちた人生を５ページ分だけでもオーバーラップさせると、なんてゆーか一言では表せない感慨深いものがあります。
lines.english: Looking at her intelligent figure, so well suited to that English-newspaper-print book cover, and superimposing even five pages of her eventful life onto it, I felt something that, well, couldn't be put into a single word.

lines.japanese: ていうか、繰りかえしますけど若いです彼女。俺と同じぐらい、いや、むしろ年下に見えるんですけど……ま、職歴を考えると流石にそれはないですよねぇ。
lines.english: And again, she's young. About my age—no, she even looks younger... Though with her work history, surely she can't be.

lines.japanese: 「なに、シュウちゃんもタマイズミ知ってんの？」
lines.english: “What, you know Tamaizumi too, Shuu?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……ううん、知らなかったけど、さっき読みはじめた」
lines.english: “Oh... No, I didn't, but I just started reading her.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 例の青い表紙を見せると、カケルくんは一度ぽかんとして──
lines.english: When I showed him that blue cover, Kakeru stared blankly for a moment—

lines.japanese: 「ああ……ああ、それか」
lines.english: “Oh... Oh, that.”

lines.japanese: ──しかし、すぐ納得できたように薄く笑いました。
lines.english: —but then gave a faint smile, as if he understood.

lines.japanese: 「え、カケルくんこそ、彼女とはお仕事かなんかで？」
lines.english: “Wait, what about you? Do you know her through work or something?”

lines.japanese: ふたりを交互に指差しながら尋ねると、カケルくんは「そんなとこ」と言った感じでついっと顎を突きだしました。
lines.english: I pointed at the two of them in turn. Kakeru thrust out his chin a little, as if to say, “Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ね、シュウちゃん。あいつにサインでももらってくれば？」
lines.english: “Hey, Shuu. Why don't you go get her autograph?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そういうミーハーなのはともかく……どうしよ、一言ご挨拶しとこうかな。実はさっき、米田さんにこの本の記事頼まれちゃって」
lines.english: “Hmm, never mind the fanboy stuff... What should I do? Maybe introduce myself. Yuu just asked me to write an article about this book.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー！」
lines.english: “Ohhh!”

lines.japanese: 「いーんじゃない、行ってきなよ。俺、ここで待ってるから」
lines.english: “Sure, go ahead. I'll wait here.”

lines.japanese: カケルくんはそう言いながらも、すっと顎を引いて隠れるように表情を伏せてしまいました。
lines.english: Even as he said it, Kakeru tucked his chin down and hid his face.

lines.japanese: 「……はあ。つまり、ひとりで行けと？」
lines.english: “...Right. Meaning I go alone?”

lines.japanese: 面識あるなら紹介してくれればいいのに。彼ったら相変わらずの人間嫌いです。
lines.english: If he knew her, he could at least introduce us. Same old misanthrope.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、それではカケルくん、参考までに聞いておきましょう──」
lines.english: “Uh, well then, Kakeru, let me ask for future reference—”

lines.japanese: せめて円滑な交流を図るため、傾向と対策ぐらいは教えてもらいましょう。
lines.english: To keep things running smoothly, I should at least find out what to expect and how to handle it.

lines.japanese: 「──多摩いづみさんって、リアルじゃどんな方？」
lines.english: “—What's Izumi Tama like in real life?”

lines.japanese: 「多摩いづみ？　多摩いづみならコテコテのギャル系だけど」
lines.english: “Izumi Tama? She's a full-on party girl.”

lines.japanese: 「あれで！？」
lines.english: “Her?!”

lines.japanese: 思わず眉間に皺を寄せて見入ってしまいました。一般的にギャル系ってーと、派手めのブランドに身を固めてメンソールの細長いタバコ片手にギャハハと笑う、みたいな女性を指すと思っていたのですが……。
lines.english: I couldn't help studying her with a frown. I'd thought that usually meant a woman decked out in flashy brands, laughing her head off with a long, thin menthol cigarette in one hand...

lines.japanese: 「仕事のときは猫ぐらい被んじゃない？」
lines.english: “Maybe she plays the innocent little kitty for work?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そっか、ここにいるってことはつまり仕事で来てんだもんねえ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. If she's here, it must be for work.”

lines.japanese: たしかに俺だって、ＴＰＯに応じてアメショーとサーベルタイガーを被りわけたりぐらいはします。
lines.english: Sure, I choose my own cat act to suit the time, place, and occasion—an American shorthair or a saber-toothed tiger.

lines.japanese: 「ふんふん、ギャル系……そんで、そんで？　多摩いづみの好きな話題とか分かる？」
lines.english: “Hmm, hmm, a party girl... And, and? Do you know what Izumi Tama likes talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「多摩いづみ？　そーねえ、多摩いづみだったらお硬い話とかは嫌いみたいよ。フランクに行った方がいんじゃない、軽く小ギャグとか挟んで」
lines.english: “Izumi Tama? Let's see. Doesn't seem to like stiff conversation. Be casual. Throw in a little joke here and there.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、パーティージョークみたいの？」
lines.english: “Oh, like a party joke?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃなくて下ネタ。マスターみたいに、セクハラ入ってるベタなの」
lines.english: “No, dirty jokes. Corny stuff like the boss tells, sexual harassment and all.”

lines.japanese: 「初対面でエロポップ！？」
lines.english: “X-rated icebreakers?!”

lines.japanese: 軽部狩男の無駄に渋い笑顔が脳裏に浮かび、俺は鮮烈な驚愕を覚えました。
lines.english: Karuo Karube's absurdly suave smile flashed through my mind, filling me with vivid shock.

lines.japanese: 「え……ちょっと待って。俺、初めてご挨拶させていただくのよ？　それはどうなの？」
lines.english: “Huh... Wait a second. I'm introducing myself for the first time, you know? How would that go?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、アリだって」
lines.english: “No, it'll work.”

lines.japanese: 「うそーん！」
lines.english: “No waaay!”

lines.japanese: 「俺んときはかなりウケてたよ、多摩いづみに」
lines.english: “Went over pretty well with Izumi Tama when I did it.”

lines.japanese: 「経験談！？」
lines.english: “Personal experience?!”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょ……教えて教えて。具体的になに言えばいいの」
lines.english: “Wait, hang on... Tell me, tell me. What exactly should I say?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、マスターみたいのだって。パンツ何色？とか」
lines.english: “I told you, something the boss would say. Ask what color her underwear is.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ごめんなさい、そういうのちょっとボクのキャラじゃないんで。事務所的にもＮＧですし、千歳鷲介としての商品価値が……」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. That isn't really my character. My agency wouldn't allow it either, and there's my market value as Shuusuke Chitose...”

lines.japanese: 「シュウちゃん、バイトったって一応はビジネスなんだから、ペラいプライド持ちこまない方がいいって。そんなん公私混同じゃん」
lines.english: “Shuu, it's only part-time, but it's still business. Don't bring your flimsy pride into it. That's mixing business and personal stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「ううう、ビジネスで親父ギャグ強要されるなんて、現代の若者文化おそるべしっす」
lines.english: “Ughhh, business forcing me to make old-guy jokes. Today's youth culture is terrifying.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、向こうも仕事用の仮面かぶってるから、遠慮してすぐにはノッてこないかもしんないけどね。大事なのはそこで引きさがんないこと。相手があったまるまで何度も何度もパス出してあげてさ」
lines.english: “Well, she’s got her work mask on too, so she might hold back and not play along right away. The important thing’s not to back off there. Keep passing her the ball, over and over, till she warms up.”

lines.japanese: 「セクハラ・ソロライヴ！？」
lines.english: “A one-man sexual-harassment show?!”

lines.japanese: 「辛い……それは辛いよカケルくん」
lines.english: “It's hard... That's hard, Kakeru.”

lines.japanese: 「言ってんじゃん。シュウちゃんは辛くても、相手が多摩いづみなら喜ぶんだってば」
lines.english: “I keep telling you. You might find it painful, Shuu, but if it's Izumi Tama, she'll enjoy it.”

lines.japanese: 「心配ならここで会話聞いててあげるよ。相手が本当に嫌がってるときはサイン出すからさ。これがＧＯで、これＳＴＯＰね」
lines.english: “If you're worried, I'll listen from here. If she really doesn't like it, I'll give you a sign. This is GO, this is STOP.”

lines.japanese: カケルくんは親指をまず上に立て、次いでひっくり返して下に向けました。
lines.english: Kakeru first raised his thumb, then flipped it to point downward.

lines.japanese: 「えー、そんな管制塔やめて一緒に来てよー、お母さーん」
lines.english: “Aww, stop being my control tower and come with me, Mooom.”

lines.japanese: 俺は頑是ない子供のようにカケルくんの腕を掴みましたが、彼はそれをはらって、サムズアップしたこぶしを突きつけてくるのでした。
lines.english: Like a willful little child, I grabbed his arm. He brushed it off and stuck his thumbs-up fist in my face.

lines.japanese: つまり「行け」のサイン。
lines.english: In other words, the signal to go.

lines.japanese: 「ちぇー」
lines.english: “Aw, nuts.”

lines.japanese: 仕方なく、俺ははじめてのおつかいに赴く四歳児の気分で席を立ちました。
lines.english: With no choice, I got up feeling like a four-year-old off on his first errand.

lines.japanese: しかし、この世の生きとし生けるものすべてにあまねく好かれたいと思っている逆博愛主義の鷲介くんとしては、心を狩男にしてでもファーストコンタクトを良い結果で終えたいところです。
lines.english: As a believer in universal love—in reverse, wanting every living thing on earth to love him—young Shuusuke wanted to make this first contact go well, even if it meant turning his heart into Karuo’s.

lines.japanese: 窓の外の白い空を仰いで深呼吸。覚悟を決めた俺は気持ちを切りかえ、真面目に不真面目なネタを仕込みながらゆっくり歩いて行きました。
lines.english: I looked up at the white sky outside and took a deep breath. Having steeled myself, I changed gears and walked slowly over, seriously preparing some unserious material.

lines.japanese: 「俺は狩男、俺は狩男……」
lines.english: “I am Karuo. I am Karuo...”

lines.japanese: その間、口の中でつぶやきを繰りかえし、不浄なる男の霊よ我が身に降りろと自己暗示をかけてみました。
lines.english: All the while, I repeated that under my breath, trying to hypnotize myself into possession by that unclean man's spirit.

lines.japanese: テーブルを挟んでいづみさんの対面席周辺に差しかかりました。俺はワンちゃん並だった速度を亀さん級にまで落とし、がしりと腕を組んで芝居がかったラウドなつぶやきをこぼしました。
lines.english: As I reached the chair opposite Izumi's, I slowed from puppy speed to tortoise speed, folded my arms firmly, and let out a theatrically loud mutter.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、目撃談だけは聞くんだけど、痴女って本当に実在するのかなあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. You hear eyewitness accounts, but I wonder if female perverts really exist.”

lines.japanese: しかるのち、ううむと思案に暮れるふりをして頭を傾けると、
lines.english: Then, pretending to puzzle over it with a thoughtful “hmm,” I tilted my head.

lines.japanese: いづみさんは読書体勢のまま、静かに黒目だけを上へ移動させました。
lines.english: Izumi stayed in her reading posture and quietly moved only her eyes upward.

lines.japanese: 眼鏡の上の隙間から、レンズを通さずに俺を観察しています。煩わしげに睨むでもなく、愛想良く微笑むでもなく、ただ壁時計か赤信号を見上げるときのような感情のない目です。
lines.english: She studied me through the gap above her glasses, without looking through the lenses. No irritated glare, no friendly smile. Just the blank eyes you'd turn toward a wall clock or a red light.

lines.japanese: つ、辛い──しかし俺は、カケルくんの助言どおり引きさがりませんでした。
lines.english: Th-this is painful—but I didn't back down, just as Kakeru had advised.

lines.japanese: 「ふうむ、やはり痴女とは、抑圧された本能的欲求が生んだ悲しき都市伝説なのかなあ。あーあ、今月の亀甲占いによれば、近日中にノンフレーム眼鏡の似合う文系痴女と喫茶店でばったり遭遇するはずなんだけどなあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. Perhaps sex-crazed women are only a sad urban legend born of repressed instinctive desires. What a pity. According to this month’s tortoiseshell divination, any day now I’m supposed to run into a sex-crazed literary type who looks good in rimless glasses, right here in a café.”
“—Excuse me.”

lines.japanese: するといづみさんが、手にしていた文庫本を閉じることもなく無感情な声で言いました。
lines.english: Without even closing the paperback in her hands, Izumi spoke in an emotionless voice.

lines.japanese: 「ご存知だとは思いますけど、思っていたことがうっかり口に出ちゃった風を装ったところで、セクハラはセクハラですよ」
lines.english: “I'm sure you know this, but pretending you accidentally said what you were thinking doesn't make sexual harassment any less sexual harassment.”

lines.japanese: 駄目じゃん！？
lines.english: This isn't working?!

lines.japanese: 慌てて振りかえれば、俯いて顔を隠したカケルくんが親指を下へ下へと向けていました。
lines.english: I hurriedly turned. Kakeru, his lowered head hiding his face, was pointing his thumb down, down, down.

lines.japanese: し、しまった、まだ早かったんだ……俺は勝ちに急ぐあまり勇み足を踏んでしまったようです。
lines.english: D-damn, too soon... I'd rushed ahead in my eagerness to win.

lines.japanese: 「あ！　いやいや、これは失礼いたしました！　自分、重度の顎関節症なもので、どうにも口の締まりが悪くてははは！」
lines.english: “Oh! No, no, my apologies! I have a severe jaw-joint disorder, you see. I just can't keep my mouth shut, hahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 開きなおった俺は、自分を徹底的なおとぼけキャラで通すことにしました。さいわいここは出版社の真下、エキセントリックな人間も多いと米田編集がおっしゃっていました。
lines.english: Throwing caution to the wind, I decided to play the complete and utter fool. Luckily, we were right below a publisher, and Editor Yoneda had said there were plenty of eccentric people here.

lines.japanese: いづみさんは眉ひとつ動かさず、意思の強そうな瞳で謎の男を見上げています。
lines.english: Without moving a brow, Izumi looked up at the mysterious man with strong-willed eyes.

lines.japanese: 彼女の小さなお顔には整った目鼻口が無駄なく配置されていて、その、ハイレベルな美少女にたいてい備わる特有の貫禄というか凛々しさに、ついつい圧倒される鷲介くんでありました。
lines.english: On her small face, eyes, nose, and mouth were arranged with faultless economy. That particular presence, or dignity, which most truly beautiful girls possess couldn't help overwhelming young Shuusuke.

lines.japanese: や、美「少女」ってお歳でもないんでしょうけど、実際は。
lines.english: Well, in reality, she probably wasn't young enough to be called a “girl.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ごほっごほっ、たいへん申しおくれました。ワタクシ、フリーター……あ、いえ、フリーライターの千歳鷲介と申しますが、多摩いづみ先生でいらっしゃいますよね」
lines.english: “Uh, ahem, ahem. Forgive me for not introducing myself sooner. I'm a part-timer... Ah, no, a part-time writer—freelance. Shuusuke Chitose. You are Ms. Tamaizumi, the author, aren't you?”

lines.japanese: 俺はにこやかな笑顔で尋ねたのですが、返事らしい返事はなく、代わりにいづみさんの桜色の唇からは小さな驚きの声が漏れ出てきました。
lines.english: I asked with a friendly smile, but she gave nothing that could really be called an answer. A small sound of surprise escaped her cherry-pink lips instead.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ……？　ひょっとして……違い……ました？」
lines.english: “Uh, oh...? Could I... have... the wrong person?”

lines.japanese: 一瞬いたずら好きのカケルくんに担がれたのかと青ざめかけましたが、次の瞬間、がたんという豪快な椅子の音が耳に飛びこんできました。
lines.english: For a moment, I started to go pale, wondering if prank-loving Kakeru had fooled me. The next moment, a tremendous clatter of a chair hit my ears.

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ！　そうです、私です！」
lines.english: “N-no! Yes, that's me!”

lines.japanese: いづみさんは本を置きすてて、勢いよく立ちあがっていました。
lines.english: Izumi dropped her book and sprang to her feet.

lines.japanese: 「すみません！　せせ、先生なんて呼ばれたことがなかったもので、その、つい戸惑ってしまって……！」
lines.english: “I'm sorry! No one's ever addressed me so, so respectfully as an author before, so, well, it caught me off guard...!”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そーすか……」
lines.english: “R-right...”

lines.japanese: こっちこそ戸惑ってしまうぐらい、いづみさんは丁寧に腰を折りまげて深々と頭を下げています。
lines.english: She bent neatly at the waist and bowed so deeply that I was the one getting flustered.

lines.japanese: それは、パッと見プライドの高そうなお嬢さんだなあ、とか思っちゃったのが申しわけなくなるぐらいの腰の低さでした。
lines.english: She was so humble that I felt guilty for initially thinking she looked like a rather proud young lady.

lines.japanese: 「や、そんなそんな。こちらこそ読書中に突然お声がけしちゃいまして、スイマセンスイマセン」
lines.english: “No, no, not at all. I'm the one who interrupted your reading out of nowhere. Sorry, sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ！　すみません！　失礼いたしました！」
lines.english: “No! I'm sorry! Please forgive me!”

lines.japanese: 一度は顔を上げたいづみさんがまたぞろ体育会系の新入部員みたいに頭を下げたりして、なんだかこのままじゃ切りがなさそうなので、俺は丁重に御着席を願いました。
lines.english: She'd raised her head once, only to bow again like a new sports-club recruit. It looked as if we'd never stop at this rate, so I politely asked her to sit down.

lines.japanese: 「本当にすみません。なにぶん駆け出しなもので、とんだ不調法を……」
lines.english: “I'm really sorry. I'm still new at this, so I behaved terribly...”

lines.japanese: 「いえいえ全然、ははは」
lines.english: “No, no, not at all. Hahaha.”

lines.japanese: お互い腰を下ろして向かいあっても、彼女はまだ肩をすぼめ気味でした。が、心なしか口元にはひそかな微笑が浮かんでいます。
lines.english: Even seated facing each other, she was still hunching her shoulders a little. But I thought I could see a secret smile around her mouth.

lines.japanese: 初めて呼ばれたって言ってたから、もしかしたら嬉しかったんでしょうか、センセーという響きが。
lines.english: She'd said no one had called her that before. Maybe she was happy to be addressed with a writer's dignity.

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、恥ずかしいなあっ」
lines.english: “Oh, this is so embarrassing!”

lines.japanese: 顔を背けて赤らんだ頬を両手で挟むいづみさんは、素が充分なだけにとても可愛らしく見えました。
lines.english: Turning aside and pressing both hands to her flushed cheeks, Izumi looked adorable, her natural good looks being more than enough.

lines.japanese: や、俺もね、世が世であればね、こんなステキな笑顔のお嬢さんと、ステキな恋に落ちたりしてみたかったもんですがね──なーんつったりして。
lines.english: Well, you know, in a different world, I'd have liked to fall wonderfully in love with a young lady who had such a wonderful smile—or something like that.

lines.japanese: 「あの……それで千歳さんは、どういったご用件で……」
lines.english: “Um... So, Mr. Chitose, what did you want to see me about...?”

lines.japanese: 一心地つくと、いづみさんはなかば俯きかけてる姿勢から上目遣いにこちらを伺ってきました。
lines.english: Once she'd settled, Izumi looked up at me from her half-lowered head.

lines.japanese: 気配りのできる俺は、彼女の緊張（してるように見えますから）がほぐれるよう、ちょっと軽めのトーンで答えました。
lines.english: Considerate fellow that I am, I answered in a slightly lighter tone to help her relax—she did look nervous, after all.

lines.japanese: 「あー、えっとですねー？　先生、メンズフリーズってご存知ですー？」
lines.english: “Ohhh, wellll? Ms. Tamaizumi, are you familiar with Men's Freeze?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい……ええと、祥玄社さんのファッション誌、ですよね。若い男性向けの」
lines.english: “Oh, yes... Um, Shougensha's fashion magazine, right? For young men.”

lines.japanese: 「そです、そです」
lines.english: “Exactly, exactly.”

lines.japanese: 良かった。女性にもわりと名前ぐらいは通ってるみたいです、メンフリ。
lines.english: Good. It seemed even women generally knew the name Freeze.

lines.japanese: 「えー、そちらの方でですね、ワタクシ、先生の最新作についての紹介記事を書かせていただくことになりましてー」
lines.english: “Well, I've been asked to write an article there introducing your latest work.”

lines.japanese: 「ほ、ほんとにっ！？」
lines.english: “R-really?!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい……あの、座ったままで結構ですから」
lines.english: “Ah, yes... Um, you can stay seated.”

lines.japanese: いちいち立ちあがるいづみさんを落ちつかせて、俺は話を続けました。
lines.english: After calming Izumi, who got up at every little thing, I went on.

lines.japanese: 「それでいま先生の姿を偶然お見かけしたもので、ワタクシ一言ご挨拶をと思いまして」
lines.english: “And I happened to see you just now, so I thought I'd come over and introduce myself.”

lines.japanese: 俺は軽く腰を上げ、改めて頭を下げました。
lines.english: I rose a little and bowed again.

lines.japanese: 「先ほど作品の方も拝見させていただいたんですけど、これがまた、とても面白くてですね、思わず口から何か緑色の粘液が吹きでそうなぐらい……って、あの先生、聞いてます？」
lines.english: “I had a chance to read your work earlier, and it's so entertaining I almost felt some green slime was going to burst out of my mouth... Uh, Ms. Tamaizumi, are you listening?”

lines.japanese: 今度はいづみさん、目を丸くして呆けたように固まっています。
lines.english: Now Izumi had frozen, wide-eyed and dazed.

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい！　聞いてます！」
lines.english: “Oh, yes! I'm listening!”

lines.japanese: 「嬉しいです！　ありがとうございます！」
lines.english: “I'm so happy! Thank you!”

lines.japanese: 「や、そんな、直角に腰を折っていただかなくても──っていうか、あのほんと、座れ」
lines.english: “No, really, you don't have to bend at a right angle—Actually, um, seriously. Sit.”

lines.japanese: 礼儀正しいというか、大袈裟なぐらい丁寧なひとです。新人の作家さんってみんなこうなのかしら。じゃなくて、これってやっぱり性格ですよね。
lines.english: She's polite—or rather, extravagantly courteous. Are all new writers like this? No, it must be her personality.

lines.japanese: 彼女はちょっとお高い感じの第一印象とはまるで違う、律儀な慎みの心と微笑ましい純朴さとを併せもった愛すべき女性でした。
lines.english: A far cry from my slightly stuck-up first impression, she was a lovable woman with a dutiful sense of modesty and an endearingly innocent nature.

lines.japanese: で──このひとが下ネタフリーク？
lines.english: And—this person is a dirty-joke fanatic?

lines.japanese: うーん、たしかに作品を見れば、そういう一面はあるんだろうけど……ほんとかあオイ。
lines.english: Hmm, her writing certainly suggests she has that side to her... But seriously?

lines.japanese: しかし疑いながらこっそり振りかえると、カケルくんの親指はたしかに力強くＧＯを示しています。
lines.english: Yet when I glanced back in doubt, Kakeru's thumb was unmistakably giving me a forceful GO.

lines.japanese: 「……マジっすか」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、なんでも」
lines.english: “Oh, no, nothing.”

lines.japanese: まあ、いいや。どのみち本の内容に触れていけば自然とそういう流れになるだろうし。なにしろあの激白体験談ですもんね。
lines.english: Well, whatever. Talking about the book would naturally lead us that way anyway. It was that frank account of her experiences, after all.

lines.japanese: 「あの、ちょっとお聞きしたいんですけど……」
lines.english: “Um, I'd like to ask you something...”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい」
lines.english: “Yes, yes.”

lines.japanese: 「その、最新作をって先ほどおっしゃいましたけど……なんで今ごろになって、あの本を取りあげてくださるんでしょうか」
lines.english: “You said my latest work earlier... Why are you featuring that book now, after all this time?”

lines.japanese: 今ごろ……？　発行日はそんな昔だったのかしら。どっちみち編集部の意向までは聞いてないですけど。
lines.english: After all this time...? Had it come out that long ago? Either way, I hadn't asked what the editorial department had in mind.

lines.japanese: 「まーほら、だって。良書に賞味期限はございませんから」
lines.english: “Well, you know. Good books don't have expiration dates.”

lines.japanese: とりあえずそんな風に答えておくと、いづみさんははにかみながら下を向いて、はしたなく緩みそうになる唇を口の内側に巻きこむのでした。
lines.english: When I offered that reply for the moment, Izumi bashfully looked down and tucked her lips inward, as if to keep them from breaking into an improper grin.

lines.japanese: 喜んでます。めっちゃ喜んでます。とても初々しい反応です。
lines.english: She's happy. She's really, really happy. Such a fresh, innocent reaction.

lines.japanese: 「あとやっぱり、ねえ、内容が」
lines.english: “And, of course, there's the content.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　内容ですか？」
lines.english: “Huh? The content?”

lines.japanese: 「内容です。ほら、ああいう内容なら、活字慣れしてないメンフリ読者にも間口が開いてるじゃないですか」
lines.english: “The content. You know, that sort of material is accessible even to Freeze readers who aren't used to reading a lot of text.”
“Is—”

lines.japanese: いづみさんの目がいったん、はるか斜め上へ泳ぎ、
lines.english: Izumi's eyes wandered far up to one side—

lines.japanese: すぐに正面へ戻ってきました。
lines.english: —and soon returned to face me.

lines.japanese: 「あの、それはどういった部分が……」
lines.english: “Um, what part would that be...?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、ええ、メンズフリーズの購買層は１０代２０代の若い男性が中心ですから。彼らファッショナブルだのスタイリッシュだの気取ってますけど、なんだかんだ言って興味あるんですよ、ああいうのって」
lines.english: “Yes, yes. Men's Freeze buyers are mostly young men in their teens and twenties. They put on airs about being fashionable and stylish, but whatever they say, they're interested in that sort of thing.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ああいうのと言いますと？」
lines.english: “Um, what sort of thing do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「ですから興味が。ネイキッド・アクトレスの赤裸々ラに」
lines.english: “I mean, they’re interested in the naked actress’s bare-all... nakeditude.”

lines.japanese: 「ね、ねいき……？」
lines.english: “Na... naked what?”

lines.japanese: どうやらフィーリング頼みの自家製英語は通じなかったようです。
lines.english: Apparently, my improvised, homemade English hadn't gotten through.

lines.japanese: 「や、ぶっちゃけ先生の作品、かなりえっちじゃないですか」
lines.english: “I mean, honestly—your work’s pretty racy, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 腰を浮かしかけて、でも気が付いて座りなおすいづみさん。
lines.english: Izumi half rose, then caught herself and sat back down.

lines.japanese: 「え……あの本、そんなに、その……でした？」
lines.english: “Uh... Was that book really so, um... like that?”

lines.japanese: 「またまたぁ～」
lines.english: “Oh, come onnn.”

lines.japanese: 「すんーごかったっすよ？　はじめの５ページだけでも、もうね、あのいやらしさは何事かと。現役中学生の男の子なんかが読んじゃったら、そりゃあもう春が来たかと思うべな」
lines.english: “It was amaaazing! Those first five pages alone—I mean, what was with all that sexiness? If some middle-school boy read that, he'd think spring had come.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、はじめの５ページって……書き出しの、あのシーンですよね」
lines.english: “But the first five pages... You mean that opening scene, right?”

lines.japanese: 「え、あのぐらいでそんな……男のひとには扇情的に映るんですか？」
lines.english: “Um, that little bit was enough... to seem provocative to a man?”

lines.japanese: 「きゃー！　言いますね先生！　あのぐらいは序の口っすか、とば口っすか、幕の内っすか！」
lines.english: “Eeeek! Listen to you! That’s just entry-level stuff? An entryway? An entree?!”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、そんな狙いはぜんぜんなかったです」
lines.english: “Yes, I didn't intend that at all.”

lines.japanese: 「うーわー、くりびつ天仰もとい、びっくり仰天！　もうね、驚きすぎて言葉が引っくり返っちゃうぐらいびっくりしましたワタクシ。先生アナタはいったい、どこまで文学界のマリリン・モンローなんですか！」
lines.english: “Woooow, I'm gastedflabber—I mean, I'm flabbergasted! I was so surprised, my words turned themselves inside out. Just how much of a literary Marilyn Monroe are you?!”

lines.japanese: 「す、すいません、そんなつもりじゃ……」
lines.english: “I-I'm sorry, I didn't mean it that way...”

lines.japanese: 「はい、謝らない謝らない。アナタは全国の迷える雄羊に、愛と夢と生きぬくための勇気を与えた！　それは紙の上の悦楽園！　誇りなさい。胸を張りなさい。高らかにその８８センチの胸を張りなさい」
lines.english: “No apologies. You have given love, dreams, and the courage to live to lost rams across the nation! A garden of earthly delight upon the page! Be proud. Chest out. Hold that eighty-eight-centimeter chest high!”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで知ってるんですか、そんなこと！」
lines.english: “How do you know that?!”

lines.japanese: 「あの、椅子倒れましたよ──や、だってほら、巻末のプロフィール欄に書」
lines.english: “Uh, your chair fell over—well, it's written in the profile at the back of the book...”

lines.japanese: 「書いてません」
lines.english: “It doesn't say that.”

lines.japanese: あれ、８９だったかな……正直よく覚えてませんが。わずか１０ミリメートルの違いでも、女性にとっては重要なのかもしれません。
lines.english: Perhaps it had been eighty-nine... I honestly could not remember. To a woman, even ten millimeters might be important.

lines.japanese: 「や、すいません。じゃあ、こちらの記憶違いでした」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. I must have remembered wrong, then.”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、それではですね、作家さんの人となりを知る意味で二、三質問させていただいてもよろしいでしょうか」
lines.english: “Uh, well then. May I ask two or three questions to get to know you as a writer?”

lines.japanese: 「……はい。どうぞ」
lines.english: “...Yes. Go ahead.”

lines.japanese: いづみさんが椅子を起こして座りなおしているあいだに、俺はいま一度カケルくんのゴーサインを確認しました。
lines.english: While Izumi righted her chair and sat down again, I checked Kakeru's go-ahead signal one more time.

lines.japanese: 監督は無言で叫んでいます──行けと。行きまくれと。セクシャル・クエスチョンをぶちかませと。
lines.english: The director’s shouting without a word—Go! Keep at it! Let her have the sex questions!
